participation.context: Held the tally at twenty-four and gave Nick no new line.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Tried a scrap and was told to wait for the yard.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Would not tick a parlour tune, and said twenty-four once more.
participation.name: Abel Garnish

participation.context: Defended the hour, and told you to leave the last page.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Showed the watchet, said the voice still held, and agreed not to decorate.
participation.name: Nick Sorrell

relations.note: the morning tally stays twenty-four until the yard hears a whole song
relations.quote: Twenty-four stands. I had it at breakfast and I have it now.

story.body: You refused to have the tune written down in the morning. You kept Nick to the words he had. You left the ending unrevised and the margin shut.

relations.note: the morning tally stays twenty-four until the yard hears a whole song
relations.quote: Twenty-four stands. I had it at breakfast and I have it now.

participation.context: Kept the heading and the crown, and did not copy a speech.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You looked at Ferdinand's name and the paper crown, and you did not write a line under the heading.

title: Looked at Ferdinand's name and the paper crown

participation.context: Accepted the spoken tally, forbade a copying, and would not answer the yard.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Said the third time had held, and told you not to argue with the holiday.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Claimed the faces and the song, and lifted the trestle.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Ticked one whole song, said thirty-five, and kept the newest lines out of the play-book.
participation.name: Abel Garnish

participation.context: Gave the health without a number of years, and stacked the inn's trestles.
participation.name: John Heminges

relations.note: thirty-five lines and one song, said, and not yet copied into the book
relations.quote: Thirty-five lines in three days, and one whole song.

story.body: You let thirty-five and one song be said. You refused a copying tonight. You drank the health with no age added, and you lifted the inn's trestle. You heard the yard and did not go out to it.

relations.note: thirty-five lines and one song, said, and not yet copied into the book
relations.quote: Thirty-five lines in three days, and one whole song.

title: Heard thirty-five lines and one song
